text.p: The Turkish central bank continued to fund banks on Monday although the cash squeeze was easier with some liquidity entering the system after the weekend, bankers said.

The bank lent 47.3 trillion lira overnight at 80 percent on the interbank, down from the 63 trillion lira it injected on Friday. Overnight money also traded at 79.75 percent. The money market had opened 44 trillion lira short.
The lira closed easier at 102,480 against the dollar versus Friday's 101,800.
Dealers said the currency market was dull due to the persisting lira shortage and the lira moved according to the dollar's gains against major currencies in international markets.
The central bank set its dollar rate for banks' compulsory foreign currency transfers at 102,350 lira at the opening, up from Friday's 101,700 lira close, and further raised it to 102,450 at close.
Yields on t-bills and bonds firmed by around one point ahead of the announcement of the Treasury's auction this week.
The central bank announced in the afternoon that the Treasury would auction on Tuesday nine-month t-bills with Wednesday value when 164.5 trillion will be cashed in from maturing t-bills.

The Treasury issued small amounts of bills in the last three auctions between November 5 and 19 and raised the yields sharply due to weak demand caused by a 10 percent witholding tax imposed on interest income from bills and bonds issued after November 1.

The average yield on the most heavily traded June 4, 1997 paper edged higher to 118.36 from Friday's 117.48. The second most active May 4, 1997 paper yielded 118.04, up from Friday's 117.21 percent average.
